ps140: Come, O divinely wise,* and in sacred manner let us honour the memory of the brother of God;* for, taking up the yoke of Christ with zeal,* he showed himself to be a preacher of the goodness of His Gospel and kingdom,* and persuades us of His ineffable providence.* Wherefore, through him, O Almighty One, grant us cleansing.

The proclamation of your words has catechized all the ends of the world;* thereby are we enlightened for every manner of divine virtue* and are guided by faith to acknowledge the Holy Trinity.* Wherefore, we beseech you, as a hierarch:* Pray to Jesus, who loves mankind, that He save our souls.

Perceiving your manner of life from afar, O James,* Christ, who loves mankind, the All-wise One who sees all things,* receiving you, ordains you as an instructor of the sacred mysteries for the people of Jerusalem* and a priest to perform the ineffable sacred mysteries.* Beseech Him now that our souls be saved.

With the blood of martyrdom you adorned your priesthood, O hieromartyr and apostle;* for standing forth on the pinnacle of the temple,* you proclaimed God the Word to be the Creator of all that exists.* Wherefore, cast down by the Jews, you were vouchsafed the mansions of heaven, O James, brother of God,* entreat Christ God that our souls be saved.
theotokion: Who would not call you blessed, O Virgin most holy?* Who would not sing a hymn of praise* to the glory of your giving birth without pain or travail?* The Only-begotten Son Himself,* begotten of the Father before all ages,* was made flesh out of you in a manner* that cannot be explained, O Woman most pure!* And for our sake, He who is God by nature* assumed the nature of a man.* He is not divided into two persons;* He is understood to have two natures* without commixion or confusion.* O noble and blessed Woman,* intercede with Him that He may have mercy on our souls.

aposticha: 1, Podoben “The joy of the heavenly ranks…”

All of us, the multitudes of the pious, celebrating the sacred feast now with joy,* exclaim with loud voices, faithfully praising the brother of God, the disciple of the Lord,* in psalms and hymnody;* for he ever prays that we be saved.

You were shown to be the Word’s brother in the flesh by His own desire, O wise one,* His disciple and an eye-witness to divine mysteries,* having fled with Him to Egypt, with Joseph and the Mother of Jesus.* With them pray that we be saved.

The choir of the apostles chose you to be the first bishop in holy Sion for Christ our Benefactor,* in that you are His kinsman and brother according to the flesh, His companion* and the heir to His footsteps, O James.

You were the brother and successor of Christ, the Chief Shepherd,* and He puts you forward among the apostles.* You loved Him for whom you died, and were not daunted by torture, O glorious James.* Entreat Him unceasingly that He save our souls.
O Mistress, accept the supplications of your servants,* and deliver us from all want and grief.
aposticha_verses: Their utterance has gone forth into all the earth,* and their word unto the ends of the world.
The heavens tell the glory of God,* and the firmament declares the work of His hands.
